result.question: Our failure mode list for transformers looks thin to me. Pull the failure modes we currently have on file for a transformer, then suggest up to 4 more that an oil-immersed unit like Transformer 1 at site MAIN could realistically develop, such as corrosive sulfur deposition or bushing faults. For each suggested mode, tell me which of these channels would detect it: hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati, il1, il2, il3 or inut. Also check whether those channels actually have data between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Recommend adding only the modes that at least one channel with data can detect, and tell me which ones you left out and why. Don't recommend anything that duplicates an existing mode, even if the wording is different, and don't change the stored list yourself. If none of the suggestions survive, say that the current list stands.
result.answer:
The current transformer list has 9 modes and is not marked complete, so your sense that it's thin is fair. I suggested 4 more. Three are worth adding and one (bushing faults) isn't. I haven't changed the stored list.

**Current list:** Partial Discharge in Oil · Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating · Thermal Fault — Core/Winding · Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking) · High-Energy Arcing · Tap Changer Mechanical Wear · Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress · Cellulose Insulation Ageing · Oil Dielectric Degradation

**Data check:** All 20 channels you listed have 4 non-null readings for Transformer 1 (Jan 15, 16, 17 and 18). None are missing. The Jan 19 reading falls outside the range because the end time isn't included.

| Suggested mode | Channels that would detect it | Channels with data? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Corrosive sulfur deposition (copper sulfide on windings/paper)** | dbds is the main one, since dibenzyl disulfide is the compound that causes corrosive sulfur. dielectric_rigidity is a weaker, later sign. | Yes (dbds 18–20) | **Add** |
| **Cooling system failure (fans, pumps, radiator blockage)** | oti, oti_a and oti_t, checked against ati to tell ambient heat from lost cooling | Yes | **Add** |
| **Phase load imbalance / neutral overcurrent** | il1, il2 and il3 for the imbalance between phases; inut for the neutral current | Yes (il1 about 101, il2 about 105, il3 about 95, inut 5–6) | **Add** |
| **Bushing fault (insulation breakdown or moisture in the bushing)** | None reliably | — | **Left out** |

**Why cooling failure isn't a duplicate:** the existing "Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating" is a hot spot inside the tank, classified from dissolved gases. Cooling failure is a breakdown of external equipment that heats all of the oil. Its signal is a large gap between oil temperature and ambient, not a fault-gas pattern.

**Why the other two aren't duplicates:** corrosive sulfur is a chemical attack on copper, not general ageing of the oil or paper. Phase imbalance isn't a thermal, arcing or oil-quality mode.

**Why bushing faults were left out:** a condenser bushing has its own sealed oil, so the main-tank gas readings (hydrogen, acetylene and so on) usually don't pick up a bushing fault. oti and ati don't cover the bushing either. The phase and neutral currents only change once it has actually flashed over, which is too late to count as detection. Catching it early needs bushing capacitance and power-factor tests, which aren't on your list. So the channels having data doesn't help here.

**Worth a look:** the oil-temperature trip flag (oti_t) is set on all 4 days and the alarm flag (oti_a) is also on. Oil temperature is only about 7 °C above ambient (roughly 85 °C against 78 °C), so the heat looks mostly ambient-driven. Separately, the dissolved gases are very high: ethylene about 16,600 ppm, methane about 7,300 ppm and hydrogen about 2,900 ppm. I'd investigate that on its own track.
